meta.purpose: Parameter dictionary for normalization. Maps every alias a lab report or JSON may use onto a canonical parameter id, with canonical unit, unit conversions, sex-aware reference intervals and optional clinical severity bands.
meta.grade_fallback: Where a parameter has no explicit 'bands', the engine grades deviation from the reference interval: <25% of interval width = mild, 25-75% = moderate, >75% = severe.
meta.band_semantics: 'bands' are ordered, non-overlapping. Each has optional 'lt' (value < lt) and 'gte' (value >= gte); the first band matching wins. 'grade' drives severity, 'label' is shown to the user.
meta.reference_note: Reference intervals are widely used adult intervals (Tietz / NCEP ATP III / ADA / KDIGO / WHO where noted per parameter). Any range supplied on the patient's own report overrides these.
meta.bands_authority_note: bands_are_decision_thresholds: true marks a band set that comes from a named clinical guideline and therefore outranks a reference interval printed on the patient's own report - 'HbA1c >= 6.5% is the diabetes range' holds whatever a lab prints. Band sets WITHOUT this flag are an encoded reference interval, and the laboratory's own range wins when it supplies one.

qualitative_vocabulary.numeric_note: A bare number on a qualitative test is reported as equivocal unless the parameter declares `numeric_interpretation`. Dipstick grades ('3+') and titres ('1:80') are recognised by notation and read as positive; those are facts about how the result was written, not clinical thresholds.

numeric_interpretation.note: A COI result is a ratio against the assay cut-off, so 0.80 is NEGATIVE. Without this block a bare number falls through to the titre fallback and is read as positive, which reported Hepatitis B on a negative sample.
numeric_interpretation.source: The 0.90 cut-off was supplied by the project owner. It is NOT derived from the Disease Master, which carries no numeric thresholds. Assay cut-offs vary by manufacturer - verify against your laboratory's.
